description: OpenPower Studio roadmap focused on standards-based short-circuit analysis, protection coordination, and arc-flash calculations, while preserving the existing local single-line editor and expanding the shared study workflow with dedicated analysis tabs.

tasks.title: Add short-circuit standard selector to the shared study workflow
tasks.description: As a power system engineer, I want one short-circuit study workflow with a selectable calculation standard so I can run comparable fault studies without redrawing the network.
acceptanceCriteria: Short-circuit study UI includes a calculation standard selector with at least ANSI and IEC 60909 options
The selected standard is sent as part of the short-circuit API request payload
Load-flow behavior remains unchanged
Existing shared-network persistence still works for load-flow and short-circuit studies
Typecheck/build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
tasks.notes: This task establishes the common product and API entry point used by both short-circuit standards.

tasks.title: Implement ANSI short-circuit calculations
tasks.description: As a power system engineer, I want to run ANSI-based short-circuit calculations so I can evaluate fault duties using an ANSI-oriented method.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend accepts ANSI as a valid short-circuit standard
ANSI calculations return fault-bus current and branch contribution results for supported network elements
Response clearly labels the calculation standard and current quantity being shown
Unsupported ANSI-specific cases fail with clear user-facing validation or limitation messages
Backend verification passes for at least one representative test network
tasks.notes: Use standards-oriented behavior and make any pandapower or engine limitations explicit rather than hiding them.

tasks.title: Implement IEC 60909 short-circuit calculations
tasks.description: As a power system engineer, I want to run IEC 60909 short-circuit calculations so I can evaluate faults using the IEC method and compare results against ANSI studies.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend accepts IEC 60909 as a valid short-circuit standard
IEC 60909 calculations return fault-bus current and branch contribution results for supported network elements
Response clearly labels the calculation standard and current quantity being shown
Short-circuit results expose method-specific outputs without reusing ANSI labels incorrectly
Backend verification passes for at least one representative test network
tasks.notes: This is the standards-reference short-circuit mode and should expose IEC-specific naming where applicable.

tasks.title: Show standard-aware short-circuit results in the frontend
tasks.description: As a power system engineer, I want the canvas and results panel to show which short-circuit standard generated the displayed values so I can interpret results correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Short-circuit results panel displays the selected standard alongside current-type information
Fault annotations on buses and branches remain readable when ANSI or IEC 60909 is selected
Any unsupported standard-specific output is shown as a clear limitation, not as blank or misleading values
Running a second short-circuit study replaces prior annotations cleanly
Typecheck/build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
tasks.notes: Keep the shared graph workflow intact and avoid persisting transient result annotations.

tasks.title: Model protection devices and settings for coordination studies
tasks.description: As a protection engineer, I want to assign protection devices and curve settings to the single-line diagram so the app can generate coordination studies from the drawn network.
acceptanceCriteria: The frontend supports attaching protection devices to relevant parts of the single-line diagram
Device settings required for time-current coordination are captured in a structured form
The backend accepts protection-device and settings data without breaking existing studies
Validation prevents running protection coordination with missing required device inputs
Typecheck/build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
tasks.notes: Define a minimal but extensible device/settings model suitable for TCC generation.

tasks.title: Generate time-current characteristic curves from the single-line diagram
tasks.description: As a protection engineer, I want the app to generate time-current characteristic curves from my single-line diagram so I can analyze relay and device coordination visually.
acceptanceCriteria: Protection coordination study can be run from the existing study workflow
The study returns time-current curve data for the configured devices
The curve data is derived from the network and assigned device settings, not from hardcoded demo data
If the network is insufficient for a coordination study, the user sees a clear actionable error message
Backend verification passes for at least one representative coordination scenario
tasks.notes: This task focuses on producing valid curve data, not only placeholder UI.

tasks.title: Render interactive protection coordination curves in the frontend
tasks.description: As a protection engineer, I want to see the generated time-current characteristic curves in the app so I can inspect coordination visually without leaving the single-line workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: Protection coordination results page or panel renders multiple TCC curves on a readable chart
Curves are labeled by device and setting source
Users can distinguish overlapping curves through styling or legend support
The protection coordination view handles empty, loading, error, and content states
Typecheck/build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
tasks.notes: The chart should support practical engineering review, not just a static screenshot.

tasks.title: Add protection coordination analysis feedback
tasks.description: As a protection engineer, I want coordination warnings and analysis feedback so I can identify obvious grading conflicts directly from the study output.
acceptanceCriteria: Protection coordination results include at least basic overlap or ordering warnings for configured devices
Warnings identify the affected device pair or study segment in clear language
The UI presents warnings separately from raw curve data
Unsupported advanced grading checks are clearly marked as out of scope instead of silently omitted
Typecheck/build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
tasks.notes: Start with high-signal warnings; full automatic coordination grading can evolve later.

tasks.title: Improve reusable network data model for multi-study support
tasks.description: As a maintainer, I want the shared network model to support load-flow, standards-based short-circuit, and protection coordination inputs cleanly so new studies do not fragment the codebase.
acceptanceCriteria: Shared frontend payload mapping supports study-specific fields without duplicating the base network model
Backend request models remain explicit and backward-compatible for existing load-flow use cases
Adding protection-device data does not break existing saved diagrams unexpectedly
Typecheck/build passes and backend verification passes
tasks.notes: This task keeps the roadmap maintainable as more studies are added.

tasks.title: Harden validation and user feedback for advanced studies
tasks.description: As a user, I want clear validation and error feedback when running advanced studies so I can correct bad inputs without guessing.
acceptanceCriteria: Short-circuit and protection coordination studies reject incomplete or invalid inputs with specific messages
Validation covers missing buses, unsupported device assignments, and impossible study configurations
Frontend shows these failures without crashing or leaving stale results in place
Typecheck/build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
tasks.notes: Keep engineering limitations explicit and user-facing.

tasks.title: Add representative study verification coverage
tasks.description: As a maintainer, I want representative verification coverage for load-flow, ANSI short-circuit, IEC 60909 short-circuit, and protection coordination outputs so regressions are caught early.
acceptanceCriteria: Project includes representative automated or scripted verification for all supported study types
At least one sample network validates ANSI short-circuit behavior
At least one sample network validates IEC 60909 short-circuit behavior
At least one sample network validates protection coordination curve generation
Documented quality checks pass
tasks.notes: Coverage can begin with focused integration-style checks before expanding.

tasks.title: Add a dedicated arc-flash study tab to the shared workflow
tasks.description: As a power system engineer, I want a separate arc-flash tab in the study workflow so I can configure incident-energy studies without mixing those inputs into load-flow, short-circuit, or protection screens.
acceptanceCriteria: The frontend study navigation includes a dedicated arc-flash tab alongside the existing study tabs
Arc-flash tab state remains separate from load-flow, short-circuit, and protection controls
Shared network persistence still excludes transient study results and tab-local run state
The tab clearly indicates arc-flash prerequisites and unavailable fields before calculation support lands
Typecheck/build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
tasks.notes: Establish the UX entry point first so later arc-flash work can land without overloading the existing study panels.

tasks.title: Capture arc-flash study inputs and working assumptions
tasks.description: As a protection engineer, I want to enter arc-flash calculation inputs and assumptions so the backend receives the equipment, clearing-time, and working-distance data needed for a study.
acceptanceCriteria: Arc-flash inputs capture the minimum required study fields such as bus/equipment selection, working distance, enclosure or equipment class, and fault clearing assumptions
Frontend payload mapping sends arc-flash inputs through a dedicated request model without duplicating the base network graph payload
Input validation prevents obviously incomplete arc-flash requests before calculation
Saved diagrams remain backward-compatible and do not accidentally persist transient arc-flash results
Typecheck/build passes
tasks.notes: Keep the arc-flash input model minimal but explicit so standards-specific calculation logic can evolve without rewriting the UI contract.

tasks.title: Implement backend arc-flash incident energy calculations
tasks.description: As a power system engineer, I want the backend to calculate incident energy and arc-flash boundary values so the app can produce actionable arc-flash study results from the shared network model.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend accepts arc-flash study requests with explicit Pydantic models and clear validation errors
Arc-flash calculations derive required intermediate values from the shared network and applicable study inputs instead of using placeholder constants
Response includes incident energy, arc-flash boundary, and any important calculation assumptions or limitations
Unsupported equipment or standards cases fail with concise user-facing messages
Backend verification passes for at least one representative arc-flash scenario
tasks.notes: Build the calculation engine around explicit assumptions and expose limitations clearly where the electrical model or standard support is incomplete.

tasks.title: Render arc-flash results on the frontend
tasks.description: As a power system engineer, I want arc-flash results shown in the app so I can review incident energy outcomes and affected equipment without leaving the single-line workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: Arc-flash results panel shows incident energy, arc-flash boundary, and key assumptions in a readable format
Relevant buses or equipment can display transient arc-flash annotations without polluting persisted graph data
Running a new arc-flash study replaces stale arc-flash annotations and results cleanly
Frontend handles empty, loading, error, and content states for arc-flash studies
Typecheck/build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
tasks.notes: Follow the same transient-results discipline used by short-circuit studies while tailoring the presentation for safety review.

tasks.title: Add arc-flash labels, PPE guidance, and study feedback
tasks.description: As a safety reviewer, I want arc-flash outputs translated into practical review guidance so I can quickly identify high-energy locations and missing assumptions.
acceptanceCriteria: Arc-flash results include derived safety labels such as PPE category or severity bands when the underlying assumptions support them
The UI highlights missing assumptions, calculation limitations, or low-confidence cases separately from numeric results
Arc-flash outputs avoid presenting unsupported labels when the selected method cannot justify them
Frontend and backend validation remain aligned on which assumptions are required for guidance output
Typecheck/build passes
tasks.notes: Keep safety guidance traceable to the calculation assumptions so the UI does not overstate engineering certainty.

tasks.title: Add representative verification coverage for arc-flash studies
tasks.description: As a maintainer, I want automated verification for arc-flash study behavior so future changes do not silently break the new workflow or its electrical outputs.
acceptanceCriteria: Project includes representative automated or scripted verification for the arc-flash request model and calculation path
At least one sample network validates a successful arc-flash study response
At least one validation case covers missing or invalid arc-flash assumptions
Documented quality checks include the arc-flash workflow alongside the existing study types
tasks.notes: Extend the existing representative-study verification strategy rather than inventing a separate testing approach for arc-flash.

tasks.title: Differentiate ANSI and IEC short-circuit results
tasks.description: As a power system engineer, I want ANSI and IEC short-circuit studies to produce method-appropriate results so the selected calculation standard changes the reported fault duties when the underlying assumptions differ.
acceptanceCriteria: Verification demonstrates that ANSI and IEC runs do not silently return the same result set for a representative network unless the match is explicitly justified by the model inputs
Backend checks and calculation paths are reviewed and adjusted where necessary so standard-specific factors, quantities, or engine settings are applied correctly
If a case cannot be differentiated because of an engine limitation, the response clearly states that limitation instead of implying two distinct methods were applied
Frontend continues to label the selected short-circuit standard correctly after the backend change
Backend verification passes for at least one network comparing ANSI and IEC outputs
tasks.notes: This task addresses the regression where ANSI and IEC currently provide the same answer.

tasks.title: Add protection devices to the component palette and editors
tasks.description: As a protection engineer, I want protection devices to exist as selectable components in the app so I can place, configure, and study them directly from the diagram workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: Frontend component palette includes supported protection-device entries that fit the existing node taxonomy and editor workflow
Protection-device nodes or attachments expose the required editable settings in the control panel
Shared payload construction includes the new protection-device component data without breaking existing studies
Persistence sanitization and study reset paths keep transient study results out of saved diagrams
Typecheck/build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
tasks.notes: Keep the protection model aligned across component defaults, editors, payload mapping, and backend validation.

tasks.title: Prevent overlapping short-circuit contribution annotations
tasks.description: As a user, I want fault contribution displays to remain visually distinct from other fault-current annotations so I can read short-circuit results on the canvas without ambiguity.
acceptanceCriteria: Short-circuit contribution labels do not overlap other fault-current labels in common study views
When multiple result annotations are present near the same asset, the UI applies a deterministic layout or offset strategy to keep them readable
Running repeated short-circuit studies still clears and redraws annotations cleanly
Typecheck/build passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
tasks.notes: Focus on canvas readability for branch contribution and fault-current overlays.

tasks.title: Correct transformer primary and secondary short-circuit currents
tasks.description: As a power system engineer, I want transformer short-circuit results to report distinct primary-side and secondary-side currents when appropriate so transformer fault duties reflect the actual winding ratio and study side.
acceptanceCriteria: Short-circuit results no longer report identical transformer primary and secondary currents by default when the transformer ratio and study conditions imply different values
Backend transformer current calculations or result mapping correctly account for winding side, turns ratio, and base conversion
Frontend labels transformer-side current results clearly so primary and secondary values are not conflated
Backend verification covers at least one transformer fault case with different expected primary and secondary currents
tasks.notes: Review both calculation and result-mapping paths so transformer-side currents are not duplicated incorrectly.
